read.sections.0.heading.back: Weather and climate are not the same

read.sections.0.text.source: Weather is what the air is like at one time and place. It can be hot, cold, wet, dry or windy, and it can change in minutes. Climate is the usual pattern of weather in a place over a long time. To describe a climate, scientists usually study at least 30 years of weather records. Look at Sunrise School. Heavy rain this afternoon is weather. The fact that the rainy season has been much wetter than the dry season for 30 years is climate. Here is a simple way to remember the difference: weather is what you get today, but climate is what you expect.
read.sections.0.text.back: Weather is what the air is like at one time and place. It may be hot, cold, wet, dry or windy, and it can change within a few minutes. Climate is the usual pattern of weather in a place over a long period. To describe a place's climate, scientists usually study at least 30 years of weather records. Look at Sunrise School. The heavy rain this afternoon is weather. The rainy season having much more rain than the dry season for 30 years is climate. An easy way to remember the difference: weather is what you get today, but climate is what you expect in advance.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: Weather is what the air is like now. It can be hot or cold. It can be wet, dry or windy. Weather can change fast. Climate is the usual weather in a place. It is a pattern over many years. Scientists look at 30 years or more. At Sunrise School, heavy rain today is weather. A wet rainy season every year is climate. Weather is what you get today. Climate is what you expect.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Weather is what the air is like now. It may be hot or cold. It may be wet, dry or windy. Weather can change quickly. Climate is the usual weather of a place. It is a pattern seen over many years. Scientists look at records of 30 years or more. At Sunrise School, heavy rain today is weather. A rainy season with lots of rain every year is climate. Weather is what you get today. Climate is what you expect.

read.sections.1.text.note: "seasonal wind called the monsoon" = ลมประจำฤดูที่เรียกว่าลมมรสุม. The simpler text explains เส้นศูนย์สูตร (equator) as "เส้นรอบกลางโลก", as the English simpler does.
read.sections.1.text.source: A season is a part of the year with its own kind of weather. Far from the equator, many places have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. These seasons happen because Earth is tilted as it travels around the Sun. Near the equator, it is warm all year, so the seasons are usually rainy or dry instead. In South Asia and Southeast Asia, a seasonal wind called the monsoon brings heavy rain for several months. In India, for example, most of the year's rain falls between June and September.
read.sections.1.text.back: A season is a part of the year with its own kind of weather. In places far from the equator, many have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. These seasons happen because the Earth is tilted as it goes around the sun. Near the equator it is warm all year, so the seasons are usually divided into a rainy season and a dry season instead. In South Asia and Southeast Asia, a seasonal wind called the monsoon brings heavy rain for several months. For example, in India most of the year's rain falls between June and September.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: A season is a part of the year. Each season has its own weather. Some places have four seasons. They are spring, summer, autumn and winter. Earth tips a little to one side as it goes around the Sun. This makes the seasons. The equator is a line around Earth's middle. Places near it are warm all year. There, seasons are wet or dry. In India, a wind called the monsoon brings rain. Most rain falls from June to September.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: A season is a part of the year. Each season has its own weather. Some places have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. The Earth leans a little to one side as it moves around the sun. This makes the seasons. The equator is a line around the middle of the Earth. Places near this line are warm all year. There they have a rainy season and a dry season. In India a wind called the monsoon brings rain. Most rain falls from June to September.

read.sections.2.heading.source: People adapt to climate and seasons
read.sections.2.heading.back: People adapt to climate and seasons

read.sections.2.text.note: "thick mud-brick walls" = ผนังอิฐดินหนา; "herders" = คนเลี้ยงสัตว์; "people who use wheelchairs" = คนที่ใช้รถเข็น. Check these read naturally.
read.sections.2.text.source: People change how they live to suit their climate. These changes are called adaptations. In hot, dry places, such as parts of Mali and Yemen, many buildings have thick mud-brick walls that help keep rooms cool. In Mongolia, some herders move their animals between summer and winter camps. In many farming communities, people plant crops when the rainy season begins. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered walkways keep students dry, and water stations help on hot days. A good adaptation is based on evidence and works for everyone, including people who use wheelchairs.
read.sections.2.text.back: People change how they live to suit the climate where they are. These changes are called adaptation. In hot, dry places such as parts of Mali and Yemen, many buildings have thick mud-brick walls that keep rooms cool. In Mongolia some herders move their animals between summer camps and winter camps. In many farming communities, people plant crops when the rainy season starts. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered walkways keep students dry, and drinking water stations help a lot on hot days. Good adaptation is based on evidence and works for everyone, including people who use wheelchairs.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: People change how they live to fit the climate. This is called adaptation. In some hot, dry places, homes have thick mud walls. The walls keep rooms cool. In Mongolia, some families move with their animals each season. Many farmers plant seeds when the rains start. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered paths keep students dry. Water stations help on hot days. A good adaptation helps everyone.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: People change how they live to suit the climate. This is called adaptation. In some hot, dry places, houses have thick mud walls. The walls keep rooms cool. In Mongolia some families move home with their animals every season. Many farmers plant when the rain starts. Sunrise School adapts too. Covered walkways keep students dry. Water stations help on hot days. Good adaptation helps everyone.

write.example.source: The records show that the rainy season has been much wetter than the dry season for 30 years. This is a fact about climate because it is a long pattern. I recommend more covered walkways between the classrooms and the gate. This would help students because they could stay dry when it rains. It should also work for students who use wheelchairs. So the walkways need ramps, not only steps.
write.example.back: The records show that over 30 years the rainy season has had much more rain than the dry season. This is a fact about climate because it is a long pattern. I suggest there should be more covered walkways between the classrooms and the school gate. This would help students because it keeps them dry when it rains. It should also work for students who use wheelchairs, so the walkways need ramps, not just steps.

watch.summary.source: This video explains how Earth's climate is changing. Some gases in the air, like carbon dioxide, trap heat from the Sun. They work a bit like the glass walls of a greenhouse, which keep plants warm. People burn coal, oil and gas for energy. This adds more of these gases to the air, so Earth is getting warmer. The video says a warmer Earth changes weather patterns. Large areas of ice in Greenland and Antarctica are melting, and the sea is rising. Some places now get stronger storms and heavier rain. Other places get longer dry times. This can make it harder to grow food. The video ends with a hopeful idea. People can use power from the sun and wind, which does not add these gases.
watch.summary.back: This video explains how the Earth's climate is changing. Some gases in the air, such as carbon dioxide, trap heat from the sun. These gases work like the glass walls of a greenhouse that keep plants warm. People burn coal, oil and gas for energy. This adds these gases to the air, so the Earth gets warmer. The video says a warmer Earth changes weather patterns. Big sheets of ice in Greenland and Antarctica are melting, and sea levels are rising. Now some places have stronger storms and heavier rain. Some places have longer dry spells. This can make it harder to grow food. The video ends with a hopeful idea: people can use energy from sunlight and wind, which doesn't add these gases.
